title: A Homecoming for the Yearbook
premise: Orsen Nakamura has perfected invisibility at Kettle Creek High, but when he finds his late grandmother's recipe box hiding coded instructions to 'The Yearbook'—a century-old underground ledger where the town's bakers recorded debts, favors, and wrongs the law never fixed—he inherits a duty he never asked for. The Yearbook's next entry is due before prom, and the current Keeper, Principal Voss, intends to erase a decades-old wrong done to Orsen's own family to bury her own guilt. Orsen must rally a found family of misfits, outbake the town's expectations, and choose between exposing Voss publicly or forging a new kind of justice, ultimately rewriting the Yearbook itself so it serves the town's forgotten rather than its powerful.
about_author: Edmund Ishikawa is a former pastry chef who spent a decade working in his family's bakery in a small Pacific Northwest town before turning to writing full-time. His stories blend food, memory, and quiet acts of rebellion, and he still judges a town by the quality of its morning bread.

chapters.title: The Recipe That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. While restocking his grandmother's recipe box after her funeral, Orsen finds a card labeled 'Honey Grief Bread' whose instructions describe a ritual, not a recipe. He dismisses it as senility, but bakes it anyway, and the loaf comes out impossibly warm. Emotional beat: grief cracking open into curiosity.

chapters.title: Locker Shut, Head Down
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Establishing his invisibility strategy at school: he bakes peace-offering muffins for teachers, deflects his best friend Dex's questions, and watches prom committee politics from the edges. When he overhears Principal Voss burning papers in her office after hours, his curiosity sharpens. Emotional beat: the cost and comfort of staying unseen.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Ledger
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Following the recipe card's clues to the old mill bakery, Orsen discovers the Yearbook—a leather ledger of debts and unrecorded wrongs kept by generations of town bakers, with his grandmother's handwriting on the last page and Voss's name stamped as current Keeper. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Flour on Her Hands
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The principal confronts Orsen privately, revealing she inherited the Yearbook from his grandmother and that a final entry must be resolved before prom night or the tradition dies with the town's trust. She lies about what the final entry contains. Emotional beat: duty wearing the mask of kindness.

chapters.title: The Misfit Table
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen recruits Dex, prom-obsessed outcast Marisol, and quiet janitor Mr. Okafor, who knew Orsen's grandmother. Together they decode the Yearbook's cipher and discover the final entry: the wrongful eviction of a Japanese-American family in 1942—the Nakamuras—engineered by Voss's grandfather. Emotional beat: loneliness dissolving into found family.

chapters.title: What the Town Owes
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The group traces how the stolen Nakamura bakery property became the land under the school itself, and how Voss has quietly suppressed the entry for years. Marisol's prom committee access becomes their way in. Emotional beat: anger finding its purpose.

chapters.title: Bread and Blackmail
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss discovers the students' investigation and offers Orsen a deal: she'll fund his culinary school dreams if he lets the entry stay buried. Torn, he nearly accepts, straining his bond with Dex and Marisol. Emotional beat: temptation, and the first real fracture in the found family.

chapters.title: The Night Bake
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. On the eve of prom, Orsen bakes his grandmother's Honey Grief Bread for the whole town, embedding the Yearbook's story in a public ritual his grandmother designed: bread that makes people tell the truth. The town gathers, stories surface, and Voss arrives to stop it. Emotional beat: courage rising from grief.

chapters.title: Prom, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, climax. At prom, Voss publicly accuses Orsen of theft and vandalism to discredit him, but Dex, Marisol, and Mr. Okafor present the ledger and land records. Orsen chooses neither vengeance nor silence: he offers Voss the pen, asking her to write the truth in her own hand. Emotional beat: love against duty, resolved by grace.

chapters.title: The New First Page
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Voss confesses and steps down as Keeper; the town votes to return the land's proceeds to descendant families. Orsen becomes the youngest Keeper, writes a new first page—'We record what the law forgot, so no one is invisible'—and finally opens his locker, and his heart, to Dex. Emotional beat: homecoming, at last.
